content: pandas DataFrame.combine_first(other) fills NaN values in the calling frame with non-null values from other, unioning both frames' indexes -- purpose-built for merging two partially-populated frames into one row per key, unlike merge() which performs join-style row combination on key columns without null-filling semantics. Source: official pandas docs (pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.combine_first.html).
